The ScreenR object class

Source: R/screenr-class.R
screenr_object-class.Rd

The screenr_object class is the main object of the package: it stores the data of a screen and is passed to the functions of the analysis. Create it with create_screenr_object.

It extends SummarizedExperiment, so it can be used with all the Bioconductor tools that work with that class:

  • assay(object, "counts"): the raw counts, one row for each barcode and one column for each sample;

  • assay(object, "normalized"): the normalized counts, after normalize_data;

  • rowData(object): the barcode identifier (Barcode) and its annotation (Gene, ...);

  • colData(object): the Sample, Day and Treatment of each sample (see get_sample_table) and its Group.

The ScreenR accessors (get_count_table, set_count_table, ...) work as in the previous versions of the package. Objects created with versions older than 1.15.8 are converted automatically (see update_screenr_object).

Value

screenr_object() (the class generator) returns a new object of class screenr_object; use create_screenr_object to build one from your data.

Slots

annotation_table

The annotation table as given by the user (it can contain barcodes that are not in the count table).

replicates

The replicate labels.

data_table

The data table, a tidy (long) version of the normalized counts (see compute_data_table).

column_names

The names that the columns had in the tables given by the user (see get_column_names).

See also

create_screenr_object, update_screenr_object

Examples

data("count_table", package = "ScreenR")
data("annotation_table", package = "ScreenR")

groups <- factor(c(
    "T1/T2", "T1/T2", "Treated", "Treated", "Treated",
    "Control", "Control", "Control", "Treated", "Treated",
    "Treated", "Control", "Control", "Control"
))

obj <- create_screenr_object(
    table = count_table,
    annotation = annotation_table,
    groups = groups,
    replicates = c("")
)
#> Warning: The count table has duplicated barcodes (*).
#> Warning: 1 barcode(s) of the count table are not in the annotation table (*). Remove them (for example the unmapped reads "*") before the edgeR based analyses.
#> The Day and the Treatment of each sample are taken from the sample names (Day_Treatment_Replicate). For 2 sample(s) (Time_1, Time_2) they cannot be separated and are both set to the first part of the name. If this is not intended, give them with the sample_table argument. Check them with get_sample_table().
obj
#> class: screenr_object 
#> dim: 5323 14 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(5323): 10208 10502 ... 13995 *.2
#> rowData names(5): Barcode Gene Gene_ID Sequence Library
#> colnames(14): Time_1 Time_2 ... Time_4_rep2 Time_4_rep3
#> colData names(4): Sample Day Treatment Group
#> data table: 0 rows, 0 columns
